The QWAmetadata class

Source: vignettes/QWAmetadata.Rmd
QWAmetadata.Rmd
library(rxs2tria)

Overview

A QWAmetadata object is a named list that bundles the metadata of a QWA dataset, either submission files or TRIA dataset files (see Submission files and TRIA dataset files). Its components cover the dataset, its authors and funding, and each level of the sampling hierarchy:

Component Description
$images Image-level metadata; a QWAimages object. Required.
$sites Site-level metadata (name, coordinates, country, elevation, topography, soil, stand)
$trees Tree-level metadata (species, DBH, height, age, status)
$woodpieces Woodpiece-level metadata (organ, sample type, sampling year)
$slides Slide-level metadata (preparation, staining, mounting)
$dataset Dataset name, title, description, licence, acknowledgements; submission files add access rights and embargo date, TRIA dataset files add ds_label, url, doi, citation, dataset_version
$authors Author names, affiliations, contact information
$funding Funding sources and grant numbers
$related Related publications or datasets (DOIs, URLs). Submission files only.
$datafiles The cells and rings files of a TRIA dataset, with size_bytes, checksum (MD5) and s3_key. TRIA dataset files only.

$images is the only required component. All others may be absent from the object and can be populated incrementally, but a complete submission needs all of them except $related. The hierarchical components ($sites, $trees, $woodpieces, $slides) are linked to $images via the shared label columns (site_label, tree_label, woodpiece_label, slide_label).

Submission files and TRIA dataset files

The submission attribute, queried with is_submission(), tells submission files (TRUE) from TRIA dataset files (FALSE). It is inferred from the components: TRIA dataset files have $datafiles or a ds_label in $dataset. Each component is aligned with and checked against the schema of its stage. $related is dropped from TRIA dataset files with a warning. complete_QWAmetadata(), update_QWAmetadata() and combine_QWAmetadata() apply to submission files only.

Building a QWAmetadata object

In normal use, QWAmetadata is assembled through the interactive metadata Shiny app, which takes a QWAimages object as its starting point and guides you through all components. The output is exported as a JSON file that can be read back at any time:

launch_metadata_app()

QWA_metadata <- read_QWAmetadata("output/my_dataset_QWAmetadata.json")

You can also construct a QWAmetadata object directly, passing any components you already have as data frames:

QWA_metadata <- QWAmetadata(
  images = rxs_images,      # required QWAimages object
  sites  = df_sites,        # optional data frames
  trees  = df_trees
)

Or from a named list, for example after reading from a custom source:

QWA_metadata <- as_QWAmetadata(my_list)

as_QWAmetadata() matches list names against the known component names, drops any unrecognised names with a warning, and calls QWAmetadata() on the remainder.

The constructor aligns each supplied component with the JSON schema of its stage: column names are cleaned, types are coerced, and unrecognised columns are dropped. Missing required columns are added as NA with a warning. $images goes through QWAimages() (see vignette("QWAimages")); the other components are only aligned, not checked: run check_QWAmetadata() before a submission.

Inspecting a QWAmetadata object 

QWA_metadata          # same as print(QWA_metadata)
summary(QWA_metadata) # identical output

print() shows the stage (submission files, or TRIA dataset files with label, version and citation), the image-level coverage (images, slides, woodpieces, trees, sites, species, year range) and the status of each optional component — present with row count, or flagged as not provided.

Individual components are standard data frames and can be accessed and edited directly:

QWA_metadata$sites
QWA_metadata$authors

# Edit in place:
QWA_metadata$dataset$ds_license <- "CC BY 4.0"

Checking a QWAmetadata object 

check_QWAmetadata(QWA_metadata)

check_QWAmetadata() returns TRUE invisibly if no issue was found, FALSE otherwise. With strict = TRUE, it aborts on the first issue instead of warning.

  • Errors: invalid object; duplicate IDs in $sites, $trees, $woodpieces or $slides.
  • Warnings:
    • a missing component required at the object’s stage;
    • values violating the schema of the stage (submission files or TRIA dataset files), and duplicate values in columns that must be unique (e.g. email, site_name);
    • not exactly one contact person, or author_nr not numbering the authors from 1 to n;
    • unknown country or species codes, or species columns of $trees not matching their code;
    • [ADD INFO ...] placeholders left in the dataset description;
    • IDs of $images missing from the hierarchical tables, extra IDs, or derived values (counts, parent labels, species_code) not matching $images (resync with update_QWAmetadata(x, x$images));
    • issues in $images, see check_QWAimages().
  • Information: absent optional components and missing optional columns.

Completing a QWAmetadata object 

QWA_metadata <- complete_QWAmetadata(QWA_metadata)

Returns a new QWAmetadata object with all optional columns added (except qc_input columns set in the flags app) and existing values preserved. Applies to submission files only.

  • $images: delegates to complete_QWAimages().
  • Hierarchical tables ($sites, $trees, $woodpieces, $slides): if a table is absent, it is pre-filled with the IDs and counts derived from $images (the same starting point the Shiny app uses), with all other columns initialised as NA. If a table is already present, only missing optional columns are added.
  • Flat tables: if absent, $dataset, $authors and $funding get a one-row skeleton and $related an empty table, each with all schema columns, so you can see the expected fields. If already present, only missing optional columns are added.

Supplementary files

Supplementary files (original/annotated images, raw ROXAS output, reference series, etc.) are not part of QWAmetadata. They are listed in a separate supplementary CSV built with compile_supplementary() and submitted alongside a zip of the files themselves. See vignette("supplementary") for the full workflow.

Persisting to disk

QWAmetadata is saved as a JSON file, which preserves the nested list structure and all component tables in a single file:

write_QWAmetadata(QWA_metadata, "output/my_dataset_QWAmetadata.json")

QWA_metadata <- read_QWAmetadata("output/my_dataset_QWAmetadata.json")

Partial submissions can be saved and reloaded at any time. The JSON format is human-readable, so components can also be inspected or edited outside of R if needed.

Empty values are written as null, and absent components are not written. With drop_empty = TRUE (default), optional fields filled in the apps that are empty in all rows are not written; complete_QWAmetadata() adds them back. compress = TRUE writes a .json.gz. read_QWAmetadata() infers the stage from the content.
